title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 142
paragraphs: Now Maiandrios son of Maiandrios was holding power over Samos, having received the government as a trust from Polycrates. Though he wished to show himself the most upright of men, he did not succeed. For when the death of Polycrates was reported to him, he acted as follows. First he founded an altar to Zeus the Liberator and marked out a sacred precinct around it—the one which still exists in the suburb of the city. Then, after doing this, he assembled all the citizens and spoke: “To me, as you know as well as I, has been entrusted the sceptre of Polycrates and all his power. Now I might make myself your ruler; but what I blame in my neighbour, I will refrain from doing myself, so far as I can. I did not approve of Polycrates acting as master of men who were not inferior to him, nor do I approve of anyone else who does such things. Polycrates has fulfilled his own appointed destiny; and I now hand the power over to the people, and proclaim equality among you. These privileges, however, I think it right to reserve for myself: that from Polycrates' wealth six talents be set aside and given to me as a special gift; and in addition I choose for myself and for my descendants in succession the priesthood of Zeus the Liberator, to whom I myself founded a temple, while I bestow liberty upon you.” So he offered this to the Samians; but one of them rose up and said: “No—you yourself are unworthy to be our ruler, being of mean birth and a pestilent fellow besides. Rather, take care to give an account of the money you have handled.”
